title: Cords — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Eurorack Panel. Keep it, take the pick or an alternate, take the category standard, or re-roll with a steer.

options.label: Eurorack Panel
options.lineage: eurorack modular synth culture — 1960s Buchla to today's scarred aluminum
options.thesis: Patch cables are the instrument: cubes are modules on the panel, every cord is live signal, and the physics is what flows through it.
options.viewport: A dark studio bench under one warm key light: six module-cubes standing, one patch cord mid-flight from your cursor, the HUD a silkscreen faceplate strip along the bottom edge, the first linked pair pulsing red-to-blue.
options.risk: Gear-dense panels go joyless and unreadable — and dark-plus-glow is the cheap trick; the toy must stay a toy, with glow earned only by live state.

raised.raise: LED honesty — glow exists only where live state lives (linked pulse, seated jack); nothing decorative ever glows.
Whole-surface pointer honesty — the bench floor answers the cursor with a breath of light, not just the cords.
Registration furniture — measurement ticks ride the cord while it is still learning its length.
Performed delight — the pulse and the shatter perform; they never merely indicate.

options.label: Telephone Patch Bay
options.lineage: manual telephone exchanges, 1900s–1960s — the ancestral plug-anywhere machine
options.thesis: A field of brass jacks and cloth-braided cords where human hands route conversations; your sandbox as a switchboard bench.
options.viewport: Cord-weight curtains the scene from the first frame: a dark switchboard bench, cubes as bakelite modules, braided red and blue cords sagging under real gravity.
options.risk: It is the most expected world for a jack product — the category's own postcard; familiarity is the trade.

options.label: Drum Machine Panel
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm machines — charcoal steel, silkscreen caps, candy key zones
options.thesis: The sandbox as hardware instrument faceplate: every state silkscreened, the only light being what is actually live.
options.viewport: A faceplate-flat HUD strip above the stage; cubes color-zoned like step keys; the linked pulse sweeping like a chase light locked to the sim clock.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — silkscreen state honesty transfers whole; but its hero is the timeline, not the cable, and Cords' hero is the cable.
options.risk: Reads as a music-app costume the moment labels stop naming real state.

options.label: Suminagashi Basin
options.lineage: suminagashi marbling — indigo and carbon ink obeying real fluid law on still water
options.thesis: The whole stage is a live material: the pointer drags currents through the world and everything answers.
options.viewport: A pale paper floor where cube shadows pool like ink; cords dragged through the scene leave marbled wake behind them.
options.case: Pointer-physics wonder matches the toy's soul — but a second GPU fluid competes with the rope solver for the frame budget and veils the jacks.
options.risk: Two physics systems fight for the same 16 milliseconds.

options.label: Raku Vessel
options.lineage: raku firing — thermal shock, carbon, and exposed clay
options.thesis: The scene as a kiln process: soot-black ground, crackled glaze bodies, one still-hot vessel.
options.viewport: Black-clay cubes crackle-glazed where cords seat; the shatter as thermal shock.
options.case: Fuses poorly: firing stages have no plug/link reading, and the world buries the jack.
options.kept: Thermal contrast — one still-hot accent discipline in a dark room.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.lineage: surrealist impossible worlds — language as weather and matter
options.thesis: Letters condense, storm, and reshape the landscape by grammar.
options.viewport: Type as weather over the stage; cords as letterform ribbons.
options.case: Fuses poorly: language-as-weather has no cord mechanics to carry.
options.kept: Scale courage — labels as environmental typography, never UI captions.

options.label: Design Annual Plate
options.lineage: design annual plate sections — uncoated stock, registration crosshairs, hairline rules
options.thesis: The sandbox as a printed plate: crosshairs, hairlines, one grotesque, a stamp of authorship.
options.viewport: Cubes registered by crosshair marks; cords tensioned like plotted diagrams.
options.case: Fuses poorly: gallery stillness fights a kinetic toy.
options.kept: Registration furniture — measurement ticks appear while the cord learns its length.

options.label: Googie Diner
options.lineage: Googie roadside America — starburst signs, boomerang laminate, neon orbits
options.thesis: The space age served all night: swooping lines, orbiting controls, neon joy.
options.viewport: The linked cord as the one swooping cantilever line carrying the whole scene.
options.case: Fuses poorly: diner grammar fights the vintage-audio-jack brand commitment.
options.kept: Performed delight — the pulse and the shatter are allowed to perform.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What cable-puzzle toys always ship — a flat pastel board of rounded props — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A friendly pastel mat, cubes as rounded cartoon blocks, cords as clean bezier ribbons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
